pred_diagnosis: Metastatic adenocarcinoma to the umbilicus from a primary colon cancer

1: Although less likely, it is possible that the primary site of the adenocarcinoma is the umbilicus, with metastasis to the colon, given the presence of a firm mass in the right hypochondrium and the irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon on CT.
3: The presence of a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma in the umbilicus, the findings on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT, and the absence of endoluminal lesions on total colonoscopy suggest a primary colon cancer with metastasis to the umbilicus.
